Camera: rotate, tilt, zoom and pan the view

Source: R/mira_view.R
mira_camera.Rd

Sets how the stack of layers is looked at in MiRA's network view. Without it, MiRA uses its default angles and fits the network to the window. Everything can still be changed in MiRA: drag to rotate and tilt, use the mouse wheel to zoom, Shift+drag to pan.

Usage

mira_camera(rotate, tilt, zoom, pan)

Arguments

rotate

Rotation around the vertical axis, in degrees (MiRA's default is 40).

tilt

Tilt toward the viewer, in degrees, between -45 and 45 (MiRA's default is 32).

zoom

Zoom relative to MiRA's fitted view (1), between 0.2 and 5.

pan

Move the view by c(x, y), as fractions of the window, each between -1 and 1: c(0.2, 0) moves the network right by a fifth of the window, c(0, 0.1) up by a tenth.

Value

A component, to add to a plot with +.

Details

Finding the values. When a plot is opened from R, MiRA shows the current camera under its zoom buttons, in these units, and updates it as you move the view. Set the view with the mouse, click MiRA's R button (Copy as R code, next to Save Session), and paste the code, with its mira_camera() call, into your script.

Limits. The same call gives the same view only in a browser window of the same size:

  • zoom is relative to MiRA's fit, and pan to the window, so a larger or smaller window (another screen, another computer, a resized or full-screen window) shows the same framing at a different size, not identical pixels. Use the same window size when a figure must match exactly.

  • Layers moved one by one (Cmd/Ctrl+drag on a layer) are not part of the camera: mira_camera() cannot set them (the R button lists them as a comment).

  • The view also depends on everything else in the plot (layout and seed, mira_layer(stack, spacing)): copy the camera from the plot it is meant for.

See also

mira_layer() for how the layers are stacked and spaced.

Other components: mira_filter(), mira_interlayer(), mira_intralayer(), mira_layer(), mira_layout(), mira_legends(), mira_mode, mira_mode_dashboard(), mira_mode_data(), mira_mode_grid(), mira_mode_layer(), mira_mode_map(), mira_mode_meta(), mira_node()

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.

# Turn the stack and look at it from lower down
p + mira_camera(rotate = 70, tilt = 15)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Closer, and moved left and up
p + mira_camera(zoom = 1.5, pan = c(-0.1, 0.05))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
